fields.title: Consent and Legal Bases
fields.keyTakeaway: Consent is one of the legal bases and is not always needed; it must be separate for each purpose and as easy to withdraw as it is to give.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: Is consent required to process order history and for marketing mailings?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: Consent obtained incorrectly is not consent — and all processing based on it turns out to be illegal. The product part here is substantial: how to ask, when, what to show.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: Data processing requires a legal basis. Consent is only one of them, and not always the best one.
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: **Performance of a contract.** To deliver an order, an address is needed. Does not require consent — without it, the service is impossible. **Legal obligation.** Storing payment documents. **Legitimate interest.** Fraud prevention, basic analytics. Requires justification and does not work for everything. **Consent.** Mailings, optional personalization, transfer to third parties.
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: Practical takeaway: **not everything requires consent, and asking for it where another basis exists is a mistake.** It creates the impression that a person can refuse, while a refusal would make the service impossible.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: *Freely given.* Cannot be tied to receiving a service if the data is not needed for that service. *Specific.* Separate for mailings, separate for sharing with partners. A single checkbox for everything does not work. *Informed.* It is clear what you are agreeing to. *Withdrawable.* Withdrawing must be as easy as giving.
fields.sections/2/blocks/7/text: Pre-selected checkboxes do not constitute consent. Consent at the moment a person is rushing to complete a purchase is formally valid and practically questionable. Withdrawal must be in the interface, not via an email to support.
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/rows/5/1: Performance of a contract, within order scope
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: Three separate consents instead of one: recommendations, email mailings, push notifications. Withdrawal — in settings, two taps.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: The first version had a single checkbox "I agree to data processing" with a pre-selected state. The lawyer rejected it on three points at once.
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: A side result of splitting: separate consent for pushes yielded a 61% consent rate versus 34% for email. People distinguish channels, and a single checkbox hid that.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Requirements vary significantly across jurisdictions. The consent setup is reviewed by a lawyer for each market.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: Consent is one of the legal bases and is not always needed; it must be separate for each purpose and as easy to withdraw as it is to give.
